The Federal Supreme Court is the highest court in Switzerland. Anyone who believes their **human rights** have been violated can then go to the **European Court of Human Rights** in Strasbourg. For this, the whole hierarchy of courts in Switzerland must first have been gone through. The Court only examines whether the **European Convention on Human Rights** has been violated. It is not an EU court but belongs to the Council of Europe.

gewusst: The Federal Supreme Court has its headquarters in Lausanne and a division in Lucerne.
Switzerland ratified the European Convention on Human Rights in 1974.

teile.einleitung: Anyone who gets enough votes in an election is elected. This marks the start of a new task, for example in the National Council or the Council of States. Different rules apply depending on the election.
wichtigste: Anyone elected to the National Council gets a seat in the chamber.
After the election, you must accept it.
If there are as many candidates as seats, this is called a tacit election.
If someone leaves the National Council, the next person on the list moves up.
Members of Parliament receive an allowance for their work.
An absolute majority means more than half of the votes.
With a relative majority, it is enough to have the most votes.

abschnitte.text: Anyone elected to the **National Council** gets a **seat** in the chamber. There are 200 seats in total. Those elected may speak in the chamber, make proposals and **vote**. The term of office is four years. At the start, the new members take an **oath** or make a **solemn promise**.

An elected person must first say whether they want to take up the office. They must **accept the election**. Only then do they take office. Sometimes someone declines, for example because they already hold another office that is not compatible. Then another person gets their turn.

If no more people stand than there are seats, nobody needs to vote. The candidates are then elected without a ballot. This is called a **tacit election**. If a member of the National Council resigns, there is no new election. Instead, the person who had the most votes on the same list but was not elected **moves up**.

With an **absolute majority**, you need more than half of the votes. This is usually needed in the first round of a **Council of States election**. If nobody manages this, there is a **second round**. There a **relative majority** is usually enough: whoever has more votes than everyone else is elected. You then no longer need half.

Members of the National Council receive an **allowance** for meetings and preparation. The Swiss Parliament is considered a **militia parliament**. Many members also have another job. In this way they bring experience from everyday life into politics. However, the office now takes up a lot of time.

gewusst: Tacit elections also happen in many municipalities, for example when exactly as many people stand for the municipal council as there are seats free.
The Council of States has 46 seats, the National Council 200.

teile.einleitung: The cantonal government is the highest executive authority of a canton. It is usually called the Regierungsrat, or the Council of State in French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino. Like a small Federal Council, it makes sure that laws are put into practice in the canton and that everything works.
wichtigste: Each of the 26 cantons has its own government.
The cantonal government is usually called the Regierungsrat or Council of State.
Depending on the canton, it has five or seven members.
In all cantons its members are elected directly by the people.
Each member heads a department, for example for education, health or finance.
The government decides together according to the principle of collegiality.
It is kept in check by the cantonal parliament.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland is a federal state, and every canton has its own constitution, its own parliament and its own government. The cantonal government is the **executive**, the power that carries things out. It puts into practice the laws passed by the cantonal parliament or the people. It also runs the cantonal **administration**, with thousands of employees such as teachers, police officers or road workers.

In most German-speaking cantons the government is called the **Regierungsrat**. In French-speaking Switzerland it is called the Conseil d'État and in Ticino the Consiglio di Stato, in English Council of State. In the canton of the Grisons it is simply called the Government, and in Appenzell Innerrhoden the Standeskommission. It is chaired by a president of the government; in some cantons, such as Glarus or Uri, the term is **Landammann**.

Unlike the Federal Council, which is elected by Parliament, cantonal governments are elected directly by the **people**. The term of office is usually four years, in some cantons such as Vaud or Geneva five years. Depending on the canton, the government has five or seven members; Zurich, Bern and Geneva, for example, have seven. Usually people from several parties sit together in the government.

Each member of the government heads a **department**, which in some cantons is called a directorate. Typical areas are education, health, security, building and transport, and finance. The cantons are responsible, for example, for schools, hospitals and the police. That is why the cantonal government affects the everyday lives of children and families very directly.

The government takes important decisions together as a body. The **principle of collegiality** applies: to the outside world, all members support the joint decision, even if they had a different opinion. The government is kept in check by the cantonal parliament, which depending on the canton is called the Grand Council, Kantonsrat or Landrat. This can ask questions, reject the budget and demand reports.

begriffe.erklaerung: The authority that carries out laws and runs the administration.
The most common name for a canton's government and for its members.
An area of the government's work, for example education or finance.
In some cantons, the title of the president of the government.

gewusst: In the canton of Basel-Stadt, the people elect the president of the government in a separate election.
A member of a cantonal government is also called a Regierungsrat or Regierungsrätin, just like the whole body.
Because the cantons are responsible for schools, the cantonal government helps decide which curricula apply at your school.

teile.einleitung: When young people commit a crime in Switzerland, a separate law applies to them: juvenile criminal law. Its main aim is to help young people get back on the right track. That is why protection and education come first.
wichtigste: Juvenile criminal law applies to acts committed before a person's 18th birthday.
The separate Juvenile Criminal Law Act has applied since 1 January 2007.
Protection and education come first.
In many cantons, the juvenile prosecutor's office conducts the proceedings.
The mildest penalty is a reprimand.
Detention is only possible from the age of 15.
Protective measures help young people who need support.

abschnitte.titel: A separate law for young people
abschnitte.text: The **Juvenile Criminal Law Act** applies to acts that someone committed before their **18th birthday**. For later acts, the criminal law for adults applies. The act came into force on **1 January 2007**; before that, juvenile criminal law was part of the Criminal Code. Young people are still developing. That is why **protection and education** come first, not retribution.

In many cantons, the **juvenile prosecutor's office** investigates crimes committed by young people. It finds out what happened and how the young person is doing. In simpler cases it can impose a penalty itself. More serious cases go to the **juvenile court**. Parents and professionals are often involved too.

The mildest penalty is a **reprimand**, a formal rebuke for the act. With **personal work**, young people work without pay, for example in a care home or for the community. It can also mean attending a course. **Detention** is only possible if the person was at least **15** at the time of the act. For very serious crimes, it can last up to **four years** for young people aged 16 and over.

Some young people need special **support**. For this there are **protective measures**. They include **supervision**, personal **care**, outpatient treatment or **placement**, for example in a home. They can be ordered in addition to a penalty. The aim is that the young people later lead a life without crime.

gewusst: Children under 10 cannot be punished in Switzerland.
Since 2011 there has been a separate Juvenile Criminal Procedure Code for proceedings against young people.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Lucerne lies in central Switzerland on Lake Lucerne. The city of Lucerne is popular with visitors from all over the world. It is known for its wooden bridge, its carnival and its local mountain, Pilatus.
wichtigste: The Chapel Bridge with its Water Tower is the landmark of Lucerne.
The steepest cogwheel railway in the world runs up Pilatus.
The Lion Monument shows a dying lion.
The Swiss Museum of Transport is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.
The Entlebuch has been a UNESCO biosphere since 2001.

abschnitte.text: The **Chapel Bridge** is a covered **wooden bridge** over the Reuss. Beside it stands the octagonal **Water Tower**. Old painted panels hang under the roof. In 1993 the bridge was badly damaged by a fire and was then rebuilt. Above the old town stands the **Musegg Wall**, an old town wall with towers. The clock on the **Zyt tower** is the oldest in the city and may strike one minute before all the others.

The **Lion Monument** is carved into a rock face. It shows a dying lion. The monument recalls **Swiss soldiers** who died in Paris in 1792 while protecting the king. At that time many Swiss served as mercenaries in foreign countries. Many visitors pause here in silence.

abschnitte.titel: Pilatus and the Museum of Transport
abschnitte.text: **Pilatus** is Lucerne's local mountain. The **Pilatus Railway** has a gradient of up to **48 per cent** and is considered the steepest cogwheel railway in the world. In the **Swiss Museum of Transport** you can see locomotives, cars, ships and aircraft. There is also a planetarium there. It is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.

The **Lucerne carnival** is one of the biggest in Switzerland. It begins on Schmutziger Donnerstag (Fat Thursday). Many **Guggenmusik** bands play loudly and out of tune in the streets. In the west of the canton lies the **Entlebuch**, with moors, forests and mountains. Since 2001 it has been a **UNESCO biosphere**, where people and nature are meant to live well together.

gewusst: The Chapel Bridge is considered one of the oldest covered wooden bridges in Europe.
In 1332 Lucerne was the first city-state to form an alliance with the forest cantons of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden.

teile.einleitung: Every Swiss canton has a capital. The cantonal government and usually also the cantonal parliament have their seat there. But the capital is not always the largest town in the canton.
wichtigste: The most important place in a canton is called its capital.
The cantonal government has its seat in the capital.
Many capitals have the same name as their canton, for example Lucerne or Zurich.
The capital of Thurgau is Frauenfeld.
The capital is not always the largest town in the canton.
Bern is Switzerland's federal city.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland has **26 cantons**, and each has a **capital**. The **cantonal government** works there. The **cantonal parliament** usually meets there too, and many cantonal offices are based there. That is why the capital matters for the whole canton. Anyone who has business with the canton often travels there.

In several cantons the capital has the same name as the canton. The capital of the canton of **Lucerne** is Lucerne. **Zurich** is the capital of the canton of Zurich and also the largest city in Switzerland. Other examples are **Fribourg**, Bern, Zug, Schwyz, St Gallen and Geneva. The capital of **Basel-Stadt** is Basel, the city on the Rhine.

In other cantons the capital has its own name. The capital of **Thurgau** is **Frauenfeld**. In the canton of Aargau it is **Aarau**, in Valais **Sion**, in the Grisons **Chur** and in Ticino **Bellinzona**. In Uri it is **Altdorf**, in Obwalden Sarnen and in Nidwalden Stans.

The capital is the **seat of government**, not necessarily the largest town. In the canton of **Basel-Landschaft** the capital is **Liestal**. But the municipality of **Allschwil** is larger. In Ticino, too, Lugano is larger than the capital Bellinzona. In Valais, on the other hand, Sion is also the largest town.

For the whole country, **Bern** is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament. Officially, however, Bern is called the **federal city**, not the capital. This is because the Constitution does not name a capital. Bern is also the capital of the **canton of Bern**. So the city has two important roles.

gewusst: In the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden, the government and parliament sit in Herisau, but the high court sits in Trogen.
The old town of Fribourg is one of the largest medieval old towns in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: John Locke was an English philosopher who lived from 1632 to 1704. He is considered one of the fathers of liberalism. His ideas about natural rights and a government based on consent influenced many constitutions.
wichtigste: Locke's main political work is the “Two Treatises of Government” of 1689.
The state should protect life, liberty and property.
If a government permanently violates these rights, the people may resist.
Locke's writings justified the Glorious Revolution.
For Locke, property comes about through labour.
The American Declaration of Independence took up his ideas.

abschnitte.text: Locke asks how people would live without a state. He imagines this **state of nature** differently from **Thomas Hobbes**. For Locke, people there are **free and equal** and bound by the **law of nature**, which is reason. But there is no **impartial judge** to settle disputes. That is why people found a state.

In the **“Two Treatises of Government”** of 1689, Locke explains what the state is for. It should protect the natural rights of **life, liberty and property**. Locke sums them up with the word **“property”**. For him, property comes about through **labour**: whoever mixes their labour with a piece of nature makes it their property. A government rests on the **consent** of the citizens.

If a government permanently violates the citizens' rights, it breaks their trust. Then power falls back to the **people**, and they may **resist**. With this, Locke provided a justification for the **Glorious Revolution** of 1688. At that time King James II was deposed, and William of Orange came to the throne. Besides the legislative and the executive, Locke named the **federative power** for war, peace and alliances.

In his **“Letter Concerning Toleration”**, Locke called for religious tolerance. The state should not interfere in belief, as long as peace is kept. Locke's ideas had a strong effect in America. In 1776, in the **Declaration of Independence**, **Thomas Jefferson** named life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness as unalienable rights. This formula is based on Locke.

gewusst: Locke first published his “Two Treatises” without his name.
Locke described the mind of a newborn baby as a blank sheet that is only filled through experience.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Schwyz lies in central Switzerland and is one of the three original cantons. The name of Switzerland comes from its name. It is known for mountains, caves, monasteries and the pocket knife.
wichtigste: The name Switzerland (Schweiz) comes from the name Schwyz.
The Hölloch in the Muotathal is one of the longest caves in the world.
The Black Madonna is in Einsiedeln Abbey.
The Swiss pocket knife is made in Ibach.
The Sihlsee is the largest reservoir in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Together with Uri and Unterwalden, Schwyz was one of the three **original cantons**. Because Schwyz was well known, the whole Confederation was later called **Switzerland** (Schweiz). The red flag with the white cross also goes back to the coat of arms of Schwyz. In the capital, **Schwyz**, the **Museum of the Federal Charters** displays the Federal Charter of 1291. Above the town rises the pointed **Grosser Mythen**, almost 1900 metres high.

The **Hölloch** lies in the **Muotathal**. This cave is over 200 kilometres long and is one of the longest in the world. The **Muotathal weather prophets** (Wetterschmöcker) are also well known. They watch animals, plants and ants. From this they predict the **weather** for the coming months. Twice a year they meet and present their forecasts.

**Einsiedeln Abbey** is the most important **place of pilgrimage** in Switzerland. Many people visit the **Black Madonna** there. Near Einsiedeln lies the **Sihlsee**, which was dammed in 1937. It has the largest area of all the reservoirs in Switzerland. The summit of the **Rigi**, Rigi Kulm, lies in the canton of Schwyz. The Rigi is called the “Queen of the Mountains”; a cogwheel railway was already running up it in 1871.

**Pocket knives** have been made in **Ibach** near Schwyz for over 100 years. The red knife with the cross is known all over the world. Besides the blade, it has many tools, for example a screwdriver and a bottle opener. For a long time Swiss soldiers were also given such a **soldier's knife**.

gewusst: The Rigi railway from Vitznau was the first mountain railway in Europe, in 1871.
The Federal Charter of 1291 is written in Latin.

teile.einleitung: Valais is a mountain canton in the south of Switzerland. It consists of the long valley of the Rhône and many side valleys between high alpine peaks. French and German are spoken in Valais.
wichtigste: Valais lies in the south of Switzerland and borders Italy and France.
The capital is called Sion in French and Sitten in German.
The Rhône flows through the whole of Valais into Lake Geneva.
The Dufourspitze, at 4634 metres, is the highest mountain in Switzerland.
The Matterhorn is one of the best-known mountains in the world.
The Great Aletsch Glacier is the largest glacier in the Alps.
Valais is known for apricots, raclette and Hérens cows.

abschnitte.text: Valais is a large **valley**. The **Rhône** rises at the Rhône Glacier in the far east of the canton. It flows west through the whole valley and into **Lake Geneva**. Many side valleys branch off to the left and right, for example the Mattertal or the Saastal. Valais is bilingual: in the upper part, **Upper Valais**, German is spoken, and in the lower part French. The capital, **Sion**, in German Sitten, lies in the French-speaking part.

There are many four-thousand-metre peaks in Valais. The **Dufourspitze** in the Monte Rosa area is 4634 metres high; no mountain in Switzerland is higher. The **Matterhorn** is around 4478 metres high. Because of its pointed shape, it is one of the best-known mountains in the world. The **Great Aletsch Glacier** is around 20 kilometres long and the largest glacier in the Alps. It is part of the Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO World Heritage Site.

**Tourism** is very important in Valais. Many visitors come for skiing and hiking. The mountain village of **Zermatt**, at the foot of the Matterhorn, is closed to normal cars. Only small **electric vehicles** drive there, and visitors arrive by train. Other well-known resorts are Saas-Fee, Crans-Montana and Verbier.

Valais has a special breed of cow: the **Hérens** (Eringer). These cows are small, strong and mostly black. In **cow fights** they push each other away with their heads, and the winner is called the **queen**. Many **apricots** grow in the sunny valleys; Valais is Switzerland's most important apricot region. **Raclette** also comes from Valais: a cheese wheel is heated and the soft cheese is scraped off.

The **coat of arms** of Valais is divided vertically into white and red and bears **13 stars**. They stand for the old districts, which were called **Zenden**. Valais has been a canton of Switzerland since 1815. Because of its many mountains and rivers, a lot of electricity is also produced from **hydropower** in Valais.

gewusst: Valais grows the most wine of any canton in Switzerland.
The Grande Dixence dam in Valais is one of the highest dams in the world.
Because the glaciers are retreating, the Aletsch Glacier gets shorter every year.

teile.einleitung: From the end of 2018, many pupils in Switzerland took to the streets for the climate. The Swiss climate strike movement organised strikes and big demonstrations and still calls for more climate protection today.
wichtigste: The trigger was Greta Thunberg's school strike in Stockholm in 2018.
The school strikes typically took place on Fridays.
In Switzerland the big climate strikes began at the end of 2018.
On 28 September 2019, according to the organisers, around 100,000 people demonstrated in Bern.
The climate strike demands net zero within the country by 2030.
The movement is organised on grassroots democratic lines and has no party ties.

abschnitte.text: In August 2018 **Greta Thunberg**, then aged 15, sat down outside the Swedish parliament in Stockholm. Her sign said **“Skolstrejk för klimatet”**, in English school strike for the climate. Her protest inspired young people all over the world. This gave rise to the movement **Fridays for Future**, named after the Friday on which strikes usually took place.

In **December 2018**, many young people demonstrated for the climate for the first time in Zurich and other towns. From the beginning of 2019, strikes took place regularly. On strike days, pupils stayed away from lessons. On **28 September 2019**, according to the organisers, around 100,000 people marched through **Bern**. It was one of the largest demonstrations in Swiss history.

The climate strike demands **net zero greenhouse gas emissions** within the country by **2030**. That is much earlier than the Confederation's goal, which aims for net zero by 2050. The movement also demands that a **climate emergency** be declared. This would mean politicians recognising that the climate crisis is urgent and checking decisions above all for their effects on the climate. Critics think the demands are too fast or too expensive.

abschnitte.titel: How the climate strike is organised
abschnitte.text: The Swiss climate strike has **no party ties** and no fixed leadership. It is organised on **grassroots democratic** lines: decisions are made at open meetings that anyone can attend. There are **regional groups** in almost all cantons. That way young people can get involved near where they live.

gewusst: The demonstration in Bern in September 2019 took place shortly before the federal elections, in which the climate was a big issue.
In June 2023 Swiss voters approved the Climate and Innovation Act, which sets net zero by 2050.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Fribourg lies between Bern and Lake Geneva. It is bilingual: the majority speaks French, a minority German. It is known for cheese, fondue and old little towns.
wichtigste: The Saane, in French Sarine, flows through the city of Fribourg.
The old funicular in Fribourg runs on waste water.
Gruyère cheese comes from the Gruyère region.
The little town of Murten has well-preserved town walls.
Fribourg fondue is called moitié-moitié.

abschnitte.text: The city is called **Freiburg** in German and **Fribourg** in French. It lies high above the **Saane**, which flows through the city in a deep gorge. The Saane is roughly regarded as the language border; people speak of the **Röstigraben**. In the middle of the old town stands **St Nicholas Cathedral**, with a tower 74 metres high. Fribourg joined the Confederation in 1481.

Since 1899 a **funicular** has linked the lower town with the upper town. It has no engine. Each car has a **tank** that is filled with **waste water** at the top. The heavy car goes down and pulls the other car up at the same time. At the bottom, the water is let out again. It is one of the last railways of its kind.

In the south lies the **Gruyère region**, with the little town of **Gruyères** and its castle. This is where **Gruyère** cheese comes from, in French Le Gruyère. Above the town stands the **Moléson**, at 2002 metres; from its summit you can see as far as Lake Geneva. Fribourg fondue is called **moitié-moitié**, “half and half”: it is made of half Gruyère and half Vacherin fribourgeois.

On Lake Murten lies the little town of **Murten**, with well-preserved **ring walls** that you can walk along. In 1476 the Confederates defeated the Duke of Burgundy here in the **Battle of Murten**. In the German-speaking Sense district lies the **Schwarzsee**, at just over 1000 metres. In summer many people swim there, and in winter they go skiing.

gewusst: At the University of Fribourg you can study in German and in French.
In Fribourg many street names are in two languages.

teile.einleitung: The Gender Equality Act, GlG for short, is a Swiss federal act. It aims to bring about equality between women and men, above all at work. It came into force on 1 July 1996.
wichtigste: The Gender Equality Act came into force on 1 July 1996.
It applies above all to working life.
It forbids discrimination in recruitment, pay, further training, promotion and dismissal.
In cases of pay discrimination, it is enough to show that it is likely.
Since 2020 larger employers have had to carry out an equal pay analysis.
Anyone who defends themselves is protected against dismissal in revenge.

abschnitte.text: The Federal Constitution says that men and women have equal rights. The **Gender Equality Act** puts this into concrete form for **working life**. It came into force on **1 July 1996**. The act forbids discrimination on grounds of sex in **recruitment**, **pay**, further training, promotion and dismissal. It applies to private and public employers.

Anyone who suspects they are paid less because of their sex often finds it hard to prove. That is why the act provides an **easier burden of proof**. The person concerned only has to **show that discrimination is likely**. Then the employer must prove that there is no discrimination. Harassment at work also counts as **discrimination** under the act, and employers must take preventive action.

Since the revision of **1 July 2020**, employers with at least **100 employees** must analyse their pay. The analysis must be checked independently. Employees are informed of the result. There are aids for this, such as the free pay analysis tool **Logib**. This is meant to make unfair pay differences visible.

Anyone who defends themselves against discrimination should not have to fear for their job. A dismissal in reaction to a complaint can be **challenged**. This protection applies during the proceedings and for **six months** afterwards. For disputes, there are **conciliation offices** in the cantons. There you can first try to reach an agreement.

The **Federal Office for Gender Equality**, FOGE for short (EBG in German), works to put the act into practice. It provides information, gives advice and supports projects. It also provides tools such as **Logib**. Many cantons and cities also have their own **equality offices**.

gewusst: The Gender Equality Act came exactly 15 years after the vote on the equality article of 1981.
The duty to carry out an equal pay analysis is time-limited and, as things stand, applies until 2032.

teile.einleitung: A court is a place where justice is administered. There, judges decide disputes and examine whether someone has broken a law. By the way, the German word “Gericht” can also mean a dish of food.
wichtigste: In court, judges decide according to the law.
A person accused of a crime is called the defendant.
Witnesses say what they have seen or heard.
A case is discussed at a hearing.
Many judgements can be taken to a higher court.
In Switzerland, juvenile criminal law applies from the age of 10.
Many hearings are public.

abschnitte.text: A **court** decides when people have a dispute or when someone is said to have done something forbidden. The **judges** listen to all sides and examine the evidence. At the end they give a **judgement** according to the law. The German word “Gericht” has two meanings: it can also be a dish on a plate.

The meeting in court at which a case is discussed is called a **hearing**. The person accused of a crime is the **defendant**. A lawyer can defend them. **Witnesses** say what they have seen or heard and must tell the truth. Until the judgement, every person is presumed innocent.

In Switzerland there are courts at several **levels**. First, a court in the district or region usually decides. Anyone who disagrees with the judgement can take it to a **higher court**. This examines the case again. At the very top is the **Federal Supreme Court**, based in Lausanne.

For children and young people there is a special **juvenile criminal law**. In Switzerland it applies from the age of **10**. Younger children are not punished. The **juvenile court** is mainly about education and protection. Young people should learn from their mistake and find a good path again.

Many court hearings in Switzerland are **public**. So spectators may attend. That way everyone can see that decisions are made fairly. Journalists also often report on court cases. For young people, or to protect those involved, a hearing can also take place without an audience.

gewusst: The Federal Supreme Court is the highest court in Switzerland; part of it works in Lucerne.
Anyone who deliberately lies as a witness in court can be punished themselves.

teile.einleitung: The cantonal police make sure there is safety and order in a canton. In Switzerland the police are mainly a matter for the cantons. That is why each canton has its own police force.
wichtigste: Each canton has its own cantonal police, Kapo for short.
The police emergency number is 117, and the call is free.
Big cities such as Zurich and Winterthur also have a city police force.
In Ticino it is called the Polizia cantonale, in Vaud the Police cantonale.
Police officers learn their job at a police school.
The police check, for example, the speed of cars.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland it is mainly the **cantons** that are responsible for the police. That is why each canton has its own **cantonal police**. The short form is **Kapo**, a word often written on police cars. Some big cities such as Zurich and Winterthur also have a **city police** force. It works closely with the cantonal police. At federal level there is the Federal Office of Police, **fedpol** for short.

Because different languages are spoken in Switzerland, the cantonal police have different names. Italian is spoken in Ticino, where it is called the **Polizia cantonale**. French is spoken in Vaud, where it is called the **Police cantonale**. In bilingual cantons, both names are often written on the cars. But the tasks are similar everywhere.

The cantonal police protect people and keep **order**. They solve crimes and help at accidents. On the roads they often check the **speed** of cars. Anyone who drives too fast has to pay a **fine**. At big accidents the **fire brigade** and the **ambulance service** also come. Together they help the injured and secure the scene of the accident.

In an emergency you can reach the police on **117**. The call is **free**, even from a mobile phone. The fire brigade's number is 118 and the ambulance's 144. The European emergency number **112** also works in Switzerland. When you call, you calmly say who you are, where you are and what has happened.

abschnitte.titel: The road to a police career
abschnitte.text: Anyone who wants to join the police attends a **police school**. There you learn, for example, **laws**, first aid and traffic rules. Sport and dealing with people properly are also part of it. At the end you take an exam and receive a federal **diploma**. After that you work, for example, at a police station or in the traffic police.

gewusst: The police often visit school classes and show children how to cross the road safely.
Many cantonal police forces also use police dogs, for example when searching for missing people.

teile.einleitung: A municipal coat of arms is the identifying sign of a municipality. Almost every Swiss municipality has its own coat of arms with colours and pictures that often tell a story.
wichtigste: Coats of arms have existed since the Middle Ages.
The study of coats of arms is called heraldry.
Canting arms show a picture that matches the place name.
The city of St Gallen has a bear with a golden collar in its coat of arms.
Chur shows an ibex in a town gate, Winterthur two red lions.
The coat of arms of Rapperswil-Jona has roses.

abschnitte.text: The first **coats of arms** appeared around 900 years ago in the **Middle Ages**. Knights carried them on their shields so that they could be recognised. Later, towns and villages also adopted such signs. The study of how coats of arms are designed and described is called **heraldry**.

Some coats of arms show a picture that matches the place name. They are called **canting arms**, because the picture “speaks” the name. **Schaffhausen** shows a **ram** (Schafbock). In the coat of arms of **Frauenfeld**, a **woman** (Frau) holds a red lion on a golden chain. And in **Rapperswil-Jona** the **roses** recall Rapperswil, the “town of roses”, together with a blue wavy line.

Many coats of arms show animals. The **city of St Gallen** has an upright **bear** with a golden collar, which Emperor Frederick III allowed in 1475. In **Chur** a black **ibex** stands in a red town gate on a silver background. **Winterthur** shows a red diagonal band on silver, with **two red lions** striding beside it.

It is not only animals that appear. The coat of arms of **Biel/Bienne** shows **two silver crossed axes** on a red background. **Olten** has **three green fir trees** on a green triple mound and has used this coat of arms since 1653 at the latest. Municipal coats of arms can be seen on flags, letters, municipal halls and often at village festivals.

gewusst: The bear in the St Gallen coat of arms got its golden collar from an emperor in 1475.
In heraldry, yellow and white are often called gold and silver.

teile.einleitung: Hannah Arendt was an important political thinker of the 20th century. She lived from 1906 to 1975 and, as a Jew, had to flee Germany. In her books she thought about power, freedom and totalitarian rule.
wichtigste: Hannah Arendt lived from 1906 to 1975.
She wrote her doctoral thesis under Karl Jaspers.
In 1933 she fled Germany; in 1951 she became a citizen of the USA.
Her main work is called “The Origins of Totalitarianism”.
She coined the expression “banality of evil” in her report on the Eichmann trial.
She distinguished between labour, work and action.
For her, power comes about through acting together.

abschnitte.text: Hannah Arendt was born near Hanover in 1906 and grew up in Königsberg. She studied **philosophy**. In 1928 she wrote her doctoral thesis in Heidelberg under **Karl Jaspers**. From 1948 Jaspers later taught at the University of **Basel**. As a Jew, Arendt fled Germany in **1933**. In 1937 the Nazis stripped her of her citizenship; until 1951 she was **stateless**, and after that a citizen of the USA.

In **1951** her main work, **“The Origins of Totalitarianism”**, was published. In it she examines National Socialism and Stalinism. She describes how **antisemitism** and imperialism paved the way. For her, the hallmarks of **totalitarianism** are **terror and ideology**. Such a state wants to control people's whole lives.

In **1961** Arendt watched the trial of **Adolf Eichmann** in **Jerusalem**. He shared responsibility for organising the persecution and murder of Jews. To her, Eichmann seemed not a demon but a **thoughtless bureaucrat**. For this she coined the expression **“banality of evil”**. Her report sparked great debates that continue to this day.

In **“The Human Condition”** Arendt distinguishes three activities: **labour** secures survival, and **work** creates lasting things. For her, only **action** among people is political in the true sense. Its basic condition is **plurality**, meaning the diversity of people. In **“On Violence”** she stresses: **power** comes about when people join together. Violence can destroy power, but not create it.

In her book **“On Revolution”**, Arendt compares the **American** and the **French** Revolutions. She considers the American Revolution more successful. In her view it created lasting institutions of freedom, for example a constitution. The French Revolution, by contrast, failed because of the **social question**, meaning poverty and hardship.

gewusst: Arendt did not see herself as a philosopher but as a political theorist.
For decades she exchanged letters with her teacher Karl Jaspers, which were later published as a book.

teile.einleitung: In a secret election or vote, nobody knows how a person voted. That way everyone can decide freely, without being afraid of others.
wichtigste: In a secret vote, you write your choice on a ballot paper.
You fold the paper so that nobody can read it.
The ballot papers are collected in a ballot box.
You do not write your own name on the paper.
Each person has exactly one vote.
Papers that cannot be read are invalid.

abschnitte.text: If nobody can see how you vote, you do not need to be afraid that others will be angry or laugh at you. You can honestly choose what you yourself want. That is why the **secret ballot** is an important principle of democracy. You can vote this way in class too, for example when electing a class representative.

Each person gets exactly **one ballot paper**, because each person has one vote. You write your choice on it **clearly**. You do not add your **own name**, otherwise people would know who voted that way. Then you **fold** the paper so that nobody can read it. You also do not look at other people's papers and you do not show your own.

You put the folded papers into a **ballot box**, a box with a slot. They stay there until everyone has voted. Then they are counted. A paper on which nothing can be made out is **invalid** and does not count.

In Switzerland many people vote **by post** and send their ballot paper in an envelope. Anyone who goes to the ballot box will find booths or screens at the **polling station**, where they can fill in their paper undisturbed. One exception is the **Landsgemeinde** in Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden: there people vote openly by raising their hands.

gewusst: At the Landsgemeinde, everyone can see how their neighbours vote.
In German, the box for ballot papers has the same name, “Urne”, as the vessel for ashes.

teile.einleitung: The cantonal parliament is a canton's law-making authority. Depending on the canton, it is often called the Kantonsrat or Grand Council, and sometimes the Landrat. Its members are elected by the people and decide on the canton's laws and budget.
wichtigste: Each of the 26 cantons has its own parliament.
The cantonal parliament is often called the Kantonsrat or Grand Council.
In some cantons it is called the Landrat, in the Jura the Parlement.
It is the canton's legislature and passes cantonal laws.
It also decides on the budget and keeps a check on the cantonal government.
Its members are elected by the people, usually for four years.
Most members hold their office alongside their job.

abschnitte.text: The **cantonal parliament** is a canton's representative body. It is the **legislature**, the law-making power in the canton. While the National Council and the Council of States make laws for the whole of Switzerland, the cantonal parliament passes laws only for its own canton. It usually meets in the town hall of the capital.

In cantons such as Zurich, Lucerne, Zug, Solothurn or St Gallen, the parliament is called the **Kantonsrat**. In Bern, Aargau, Thurgau, the Grisons, Basel-Stadt and Valais it is called the **Grand Council** (Grosser Rat), in French-speaking Switzerland the Grand Conseil and in Ticino the Gran Consiglio. In Uri, Glarus, Nidwalden and Basel-Landschaft it is called the Landrat. The canton of Jura simply calls its parliament the Parlement.

The cantonal parliament passes cantonal **laws**, for example on schools, the police, hospitals or taxes. Every year it decides on the **budget** and approves the canton's accounts. It keeps a check on the cantonal government and can give it instructions through procedural requests. In many cantons it also elects the judges of the cantonal courts.

The members are elected by the people, usually every four years and by **proportional representation**. The parties receive as many seats as match their share of the vote. With 180 seats, the canton of Zurich has one of the largest cantonal parliaments; Bern has 160 seats. Small cantons have far fewer members.

The members of a cantonal parliament are not professional politicians. They also work, for example, as teachers, farmers, doctors or business owners, which is why it is called a **militia parliament**. They receive an allowance for meetings. Many future members of the National Council began their careers in the cantonal parliament.

begriffe.erklaerung: The law-making power, meaning the parliament.
An electoral system in which seats are distributed according to the parties' share of the vote.
A plan of how much money will be taken in and spent in the coming year.
A group of members of parliament from the same or similar parties.

gewusst: In the cantons of Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden the Landsgemeinde has the last word, but there is still a cantonal parliament there too.
Cantonal parliaments often include very young members who were elected just after their 18th birthday.
Many cantonal parliaments meet in historic town halls that are several hundred years old.

teile.einleitung: In a municipal merger, two or more municipalities join together to form a new municipality. In Switzerland this has happened often in recent decades.
wichtigste: In a municipal merger, several municipalities become one.
Voters vote on a merger.
After a merger there are fewer municipalities, but the villages remain.
In 2011 the canton of Glarus merged its 25 municipalities into three.
Mergers usually come into effect on 1 January.
Around 1850 Switzerland had 3203 municipalities.

abschnitte.text: In a **municipal merger**, two or more municipalities join together. The previous municipalities then no longer exist; there is only one new one. But the **villages** with their houses stay where they are. What is combined is mainly the **administration**, the municipal council and the finances. The new municipality often gets a **new name**; sometimes it keeps an old one.

Small municipalities sometimes find it hard to find people for public offices. Tasks such as schools, water supply or building control are also becoming more and more demanding. Together, municipalities can **carry out these tasks better** and save money. Opponents, on the other hand, fear that people will have less say and that a village will lose its independence.

As a rule, the **voters** of the municipalities involved vote on a merger. If all say yes, the merger is prepared. It usually comes into effect on **1 January**, so that the new municipality can start with its own budget.

abschnitte.titel: Glarus and the whole of Switzerland
abschnitte.text: A particularly big step was taken in the **canton of Glarus**: in 2011 its 25 municipalities were merged into just three. They are called **Glarus**, **Glarus Nord** and **Glarus Süd**. In 1850, shortly after the founding of the federal state, there were **3203 municipalities** in Switzerland. Since then the number has fallen sharply because of mergers.

gewusst: Since 2011 Glarus has had fewer municipalities than almost any other canton.
After a merger, a village can still keep its name as a district.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland and has existed since 1 January 1979. It came about through a popular vote in which areas separated from the canton of Bern. The French-speaking canton in the north-west of Switzerland is known for its Jura pastures, the Franches-Montagnes horses and the River Doubs.
wichtigste: The canton of Jura is the youngest of the 26 Swiss cantons.
It came about through a popular vote in which areas separated from the canton of Bern.
It was officially founded on 1 January 1979.
The capital is Delémont, in German Delsberg.
The official language is French.
Since 1 January 2026 the town of Moutier has also belonged to the canton of Jura.
The canton borders France, Basel-Landschaft, Solothurn and Bern.

abschnitte.text: The canton of Jura lies in the north-west of Switzerland in the **Jura mountains** and has a long border with France. It has three districts: Delémont, Porrentruy and the Franches-Montagnes, in German Freiberge. The Franches-Montagnes are a wide high plateau with pastures, fir trees and moors. In the south, the **Doubs** flows through a deep gorge, on which lies the pretty little town of Saint-Ursanne.

For centuries the area belonged to the **Prince-Bishopric of Basel**, whose bishops lived in Porrentruy. At the Congress of Vienna in 1815, it was given to the canton of Bern. The French-speaking and mainly Catholic people of the Jura often did not feel at home in German-speaking, Protestant Bern. That is why the movement for a canton of their own grew after the Second World War.

On 23 June 1974 the people of the Jura narrowly voted for a canton of their own in a **popular vote**. In further votes, the individual districts and municipalities decided whether they wanted to belong to it. The three southern districts stayed with Bern and today form the Bernese Jura. On 24 September 1978 the people and the cantons of the whole of Switzerland clearly approved, and on 1 January 1979 the new canton was founded.

The Jura question remained an issue for a long time. In 2021 the town of **Moutier** in the Bernese Jura voted to move to the canton of Jura. After further votes and the approval of the federal Parliament, Moutier has belonged to the canton of Jura since 1 January 2026. This peaceful change through votes is seen as an example of Swiss democracy.

The Jura has many small businesses in the **watch industry** and precision engineering. The region is also known for farming and for the Franches-Montagnes horses, the only horse breed that originally comes from Switzerland. Every August the Marché-Concours, a big horse festival with races, takes place in Saignelégier. Also typical of the Jura is the Damassine, a small red plum.

In **Porrentruy** stands the castle of the former Prince-Bishops of Basel. Saint-Ursanne on the Doubs is a medieval little town with a beautiful collegiate church and an old stone bridge. In Réclère there are stalactite caves and a park with dinosaurs. Many real dinosaur footprints have also been found near Porrentruy.

begriffe.erklaerung: The long dispute about whether the Jura should belong to Bern or be a canton of its own.
An area ruled by a bishop as if he were a prince.
A vote in which those entitled to vote decide directly.
A strong, friendly breed of horse from the Franches-Montagnes in the Jura.

gewusst: The canton of Jura calls its government the “Gouvernement” and its parliament simply the “Parlement”.
The canton of Jura is one of the cantons in which foreigners may vote at municipal level.
The founding of the canton of Jura was the only founding of a new canton since the federal state of 1848.

teile.einleitung: The rubbish bag is the bag for waste that cannot be recycled. In many Swiss municipalities it costs money. This pays for the collection and burning of the rubbish.
wichtigste: Only waste that cannot be recycled goes into the rubbish bag.
Glass, paper, batteries and much more are collected separately.
The official bag or a fee sticker pays for disposal.
The rubbish collection picks up the bags from the street on collection day.
The rubbish is burned in a waste incineration plant.
Burning rubbish in the garden is forbidden in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Only waste that cannot be **recycled** goes into the **rubbish bag**. This includes, for example, dirty packaging or broken objects. **Glass**, **paper**, cardboard, PET bottles, **batteries** and aluminium are collected separately. This is called **recycling**. That way there is less rubbish, and valuable materials can be used again.

In many municipalities you have to buy an official **fee bag**. This **bag fee** pays for the collection and burning of the rubbish. Those who produce more rubbish pay more. This is called the **polluter pays principle**. In some municipalities you stick a **fee sticker** on a normal bag instead. In the city of Zurich the official bag is called the **“Züri-Sack”**.

The **rubbish collection** drives through the municipality with a bin lorry. It picks up the bags from the street on **collection day**. You only put the bag out on that day. Otherwise animals such as **foxes** or **crows** can tear the bag open and scatter the rubbish. The municipality's waste calendar shows when the collection comes.

abschnitte.titel: From rubbish to electricity and heat
abschnitte.text: The bin lorry takes the rubbish to a **waste incineration plant**, KVA for short. There it is burned at high temperatures. The **exhaust gases** are cleaned thoroughly before they come out of the chimney. Burning produces a lot of **heat**. The plant uses it to produce **electricity** and heat for warming homes, so-called **district heating**.

abschnitte.titel: Do not burn it in the garden
abschnitte.text: Burning rubbish in the **garden** is **forbidden** in Switzerland. It produces **poisonous gases** that harm people, animals and nature. A small fire in the garden burns much less well than a plant and has no filter. That is why rubbish always belongs in the rubbish bag or in recycling. Since 2000, combustible waste may also no longer be dumped in **landfills** in Switzerland.

gewusst: Even the ash from the incineration plant is still used: metals such as iron and copper are recovered from it.
Switzerland is one of the countries that produce a particularly large amount of rubbish per person, but it also recycles a lot.

teile.einleitung: Children's rights are rights that all children all over the world have, no matter where they come from or how they live. They are set out in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, which was adopted in 1989. They make sure that children are protected and may learn, play and have a say.
wichtigste: Children's rights apply to everyone under the age of 18.
The UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child on 20 November 1989.
That is why 20 November is Universal Children's Day, the international day of children's rights.
The Convention has applied to Switzerland since 1997.
Children's rights include the right to protection, to education, to play and to have a say.
UNICEF is the UN organisation that works especially for children.
In Switzerland children can call 147 if they are worried.

abschnitte.titel: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
abschnitte.text: The **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** is an international treaty with 54 articles. The UN General Assembly adopted it on 20 November 1989. Almost all the countries in the world have signed it and made it valid, more than for any other human rights treaty. According to the Convention, every person under 18 is, as a rule, considered a child.

Children have a **right to protection** from violence, exploitation and neglect. They have a right to education, to health, to a name and to a nationality. The **right to play**, to rest and to have free time is also in the Convention. An important principle is that in all decisions, the best interests of the child, the **child's welfare**, should come first.

The **right to have a say** means that children may give their opinion on important matters that affect them. Adults should take this opinion seriously and take it into account according to the child's age and maturity. This applies, for example, in the family, at school or when parents divorce. Many Swiss municipalities and cantons have **children's and youth parliaments** for this.

Switzerland adopted the Convention in 1997, and it has applied here ever since. The Federal Constitution already says that children and young people are entitled to special **protection** and support. If they are worried, are in a conflict or face violence, children and young people can call or write to Pro Juventute on **147** free of charge, around the clock. Teachers, school social workers and the child protection authorities can also help.

The most important organisation is **UNICEF**, the United Nations children's agency, founded in 1946. UNICEF helps children in need with vaccinations, clean water, schools and protection. A UN committee in Geneva regularly checks whether countries are respecting children's rights. Many other aid organisations, such as Save the Children or Terre des hommes, are also involved.

In the past, many children had to work hard and had hardly any rights. After the First World War, the British woman Eglantyne Jebb campaigned for children and founded the organisation Save the Children. In 1924 the League of Nations in Geneva adopted the **Geneva Declaration** of the Rights of the Child. It was an important forerunner of today's Convention on the Rights of the Child.

begriffe.erklaerung: A treaty between many states that everyone should keep to.
The United Nations children's agency.
What is best for a child and good for them.
The right to give your opinion and be heard.

gewusst: The Convention on the Rights of the Child is the human rights treaty that the most states in the world have adopted.
You can reach 147 not only by phone but also by text message, chat or email.
As early as 1924, a first declaration on the rights of the child was adopted in Geneva.

teile.einleitung: A children's municipal council is a group of children from a municipality who talk about topics that affect children. It works in a similar way to the adults' municipal council. That way children can have a say even though they are not yet allowed to vote.
wichtigste: Children from a municipality sit on the children's municipal council.
It is modelled on the adults' municipal council.
The children often elect the members in the schools.
It meets several times a year.
Sometimes it receives a small budget for its own projects.
It often presents its ideas to the mayor.

abschnitte.text: A **children's municipal council** is a group of children from a municipality. They talk about topics that affect **children**. Children are not yet allowed to take part in municipal elections and votes. But on the children's municipal council they can still contribute their **opinion**. In this way they learn early on how **democracy** works in the municipality.

The children's municipal council is modelled on the adults' **municipal council**. There are meetings, agenda items and votes. The children often elect in the **schools** who will go on the children's municipal council. That way the body is fairly made up. The council meets **several times a year**. There it plans its projects.

Children know their municipality well, for example their route to school and the playgrounds. Because they often get about by **bike**, they want **safe cycle paths**. Other ideas are a new piece of play equipment, more bins or a festival for children. Some children's municipal councils receive a **small budget** from the municipality. With it they can carry out small projects of their own.

A children's municipal council presents its ideas to the municipality's **adults**. For this it often meets the **mayor**. The adults listen and check what can be put into practice. Not every idea is carried out straight away. But the children find out how decisions are made in a municipality.

gewusst: In some municipalities the children's municipal council may meet once a year in the real municipal council chamber.
The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child says that children should be heard on matters that affect them.

teile.einleitung: The Grisons (Graubünden) is the largest canton in Switzerland. It lies in the south-east and consists almost entirely of mountains and valleys. Three languages are spoken here: German, Romansh and Italian.
wichtigste: By area, the Grisons is the largest canton in Switzerland.
The highest mountain is Piz Bernina, at around 4049 metres.
Switzerland's only national park lies in the Engadine near Zernez.
The Rhaetian Railway runs red trains through the mountains.
The heraldic animal is the ibex.

abschnitte.text: The capital is **Chur**. The Grisons is the only **trilingual** canton in Switzerland. Besides German and Italian, **Romansh** is spoken here. This language comes from the Latin of the Romans. It has several forms, for example Sursilvan and Vallader. The **coat of arms** includes the **ibex**, which also lives in the mountains of the Grisons.

abschnitte.titel: Mountains, the Rhine and the National Park
abschnitte.text: The highest mountain is **Piz Bernina**, at around 4049 metres. It is the only four-thousand-metre peak in the Eastern Alps. The **Vorderrhein** and **Hinterrhein** rise in the mountains of the Grisons and flow together near Reichenau to form the **Rhine**. The **Swiss National Park** lies in the Engadine near Zernez. It was founded in 1914; there nature may develop freely.

The **Rhaetian Railway** runs red trains over many bridges and through tunnels. A famous structure is the **Landwasser Viaduct** near Filisur. The Albula and Bernina lines have been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 2008. On the Bernina line, the train travels without a rack over the Bernina Pass to Tirano in Italy.

**St Moritz** in the Upper Engadine hosted the Winter Olympics in **1928** and **1948**. Every year between Christmas and New Year's Eve, **Davos** hosts the **Spengler Cup**, one of the oldest ice hockey tournaments in the world. A sweet speciality is the **Engadine nut tart** (Bündner Nusstorte). It is filled with walnuts and caramel.

gewusst: The Grisons has around 150 valleys.
Romansh has been a national language of Switzerland since 1938.

teile.einleitung: Every year on 20 November it is Universal Children's Day, the international day of children's rights. It recalls the Convention on the Rights of the Child, which the UN adopted on this date in 1989. On this day, people all over the world draw attention to children's rights.
wichtigste: Children's Rights Day is on 20 November every year.
It recalls the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child of 1989.
It is marked all over the world.
In Switzerland it is not a public holiday but a normal school day.
Many school classes talk about children's rights on this day.
In the UNICEF campaign, many buildings are lit up blue.

abschnitte.titel: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
abschnitte.text: On **20 November 1989** the **UN** adopted the **Convention on the Rights of the Child**. It sets out the rights that all children have, for example to protection, education, health and having a say. Almost all the states in the world have signed it. **Switzerland** joined it in 1997. On Children's Rights Day 2025, the Convention was 36 years old.

abschnitte.titel: A day for the whole world
abschnitte.text: Children's Rights Day takes place **once a year**, always on the same date. It is an **international day** and is marked in many countries. In Switzerland it is a **day of remembrance**, but not a public holiday. If it falls on a weekday, children go to school as normal. Many organisations invite people to events.

Many **school classes** talk about children's rights on this day. They paint pictures, write texts or organise small activities. In this way children get to know their rights. This is important, because only those who know their rights can also **claim** them. Adults should also find out what rights children have.

The children's charity **UNICEF** organises the **#GoBlue** campaign. On Children's Rights Day, buildings, bridges and towers are lit up **blue**. Blue is UNICEF's colour. In this way cities all over the world send a visible signal for children. Many municipalities in Switzerland take part too.

gewusst: The Convention on the Rights of the Child applies to everyone under the age of 18.
The Convention on the Rights of the Child is the human rights treaty that the most states in the world have joined.

teile.einleitung: In a show of hands, people vote by raising their hand. This is how decisions are made at many municipal assemblies and at the Landsgemeinde. The method is simple, open and quick.
wichtigste: In a show of hands, you raise your hand to vote.
First people are asked for the yes votes, then for the no votes.
Each person votes only for themselves.
Guests may watch but may not vote.
Vote counters count the hands, especially when it is close.
Before the vote you may give your opinion and make proposals.

abschnitte.titel: How a show of hands works
abschnitte.text: In a **show of hands**, people vote with a raised hand. The chair first asks: who is in favour? Then everyone voting **yes** raises their hand. Next the chair asks for the **no votes**, and the others raise their hand. You keep your hand up until the votes have been **counted**. At the **Landsgemeinde**, the Landammann asks in this way.

In many Swiss municipalities the **municipal assembly** decides important questions. Before the vote, you can ask to speak and **give your opinion**. Every voter may also make a **proposal** of their own. Then the assembly votes on it. That way everyone hears what speaks for or against something.

Only **people entitled to vote** may vote. Each person votes **only for themselves**. So you may not raise your hand for a friend who is ill. Guests may watch but sit in special **guest seats**. In some municipalities voters receive a **voting card** at the entrance, which they hold up when voting.

The **vote counters** count the raised hands. With 3 rows of 12 hands each, for example, there are 36 hands. If 52 people raise their hand for yes and 38 for no, yes has 14 hands more. If the result is clear, there is no need to count exactly. The vote counters are especially important when it is **close**. Then every vote counts.

A show of hands is an **open vote**: everyone can see how the others vote. This is quick and transparent. But some people think it can create pressure. That is why an assembly can often also decide to hold a **secret vote**. In votes at the ballot box, your vote always remains secret.

gewusst: Landsgemeinden with a show of hands still exist today in the cantons of Glarus and Appenzell Innerrhoden.
At the Landsgemeinde the crowd is often so large that the Landammann can only estimate the majority.

teile.einleitung: Ticino is the southernmost canton in Switzerland. It lies south of the Alps, and Italian is spoken there. Because of its mild climate, it is called Switzerland's sun terrace.
wichtigste: The canton is named after the River Ticino.
The capital is Bellinzona; the largest town is Lugano.
The three castles of Bellinzona have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000.
The Gotthard Base Tunnel ends in the south at Bodio in Ticino.
At the Locarno Film Festival, the best film wins the Golden Leopard.

abschnitte.text: Ticino lies south of the Alps and has a **mild climate**. The sun shines often, and **palm trees** even grow by the lakes. That is why Ticino is called Switzerland's **sun terrace**. The canton is named after the River **Ticino**, called Tessin in German. It flows through the canton into **Lake Maggiore**. Ticino has been a separate canton since **1803**.

The capital is **Bellinzona**. Three medieval **castles** stand there: Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro. They have been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 2000. The largest town is **Lugano**, on Lake Lugano. Locarno lies on **Lake Maggiore**, but most of this lake belongs to **Italy**.

The **Gotthard Base Tunnel** is **57 kilometres** long. It runs from Erstfeld in the canton of Uri to **Bodio** in Ticino. Since 2016 trains have travelled deep under the Alps. It is the longest railway tunnel in the world. This makes the journey from northern Switzerland to Ticino much quicker.

Every August the **Locarno Film Festival** takes place. Many films are shown in the evening in the open air on the **Piazza Grande**. The best film wins the **Golden Leopard**. On **Monte San Giorgio**, many **fossils** have been found from the time when there was a sea there, including fish and reptiles. The mountain is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gewusst: Ticino is the only canton in which Italian is the only official language.
Typical Ticino stone houses are called rustici.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is made up of 26 cantons. A canton is a part of Switzerland with its own government, parliament, laws and courts. Because the cantons decide so much for themselves, Switzerland is called a federal state.
wichtigste: Switzerland has 26 cantons.
A canton is a part of Switzerland with its own government.
Six cantons have only half a cantonal vote and each send one person instead of two to the Council of States.
The cantons are responsible for many areas, such as schools, police, hospitals and taxes.
The largest canton is the Grisons, the smallest Basel-Stadt.
The most people live in the canton of Zurich, the fewest in Appenzell Innerrhoden.
The youngest canton is the Jura, founded in 1979.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland is a **federal state** made up of 26 cantons. According to the Federal Constitution, the cantons are sovereign, except where the Constitution limits their power. Every canton has its own **constitution**, a parliament, a government and courts. Every canton also has a capital, for example Bern, Lausanne, Bellinzona or Chur.

The Confederation began in 1291 with the alliance of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. By 1513 it had grown to 13 members. After the time of Napoleon, cantons such as Aargau, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud joined in 1803, and Valais, Neuchâtel and Geneva in 1815. With the Federal Constitution of 1848, the loose confederation of states became today's **federal state**, and in 1979 the Jura joined as the youngest canton.

The cantons are very different. The **Grisons**, with around 7100 square kilometres, is the largest canton; Basel-Stadt, with only about 37 square kilometres, is the smallest. In 2024 around 1.6 million people lived in the canton of Zurich, and only about 16,000 in Appenzell Innerrhoden. Even so, Zurich and Uri send the same number of people to the Council of States: two.

Most cantons are **German-speaking**; Geneva, Vaud, Neuchâtel and Jura are French-speaking, and Ticino is Italian-speaking. Bern, Fribourg and Valais are bilingual. The Grisons is even trilingual, because German, Romansh and Italian are spoken there. In this way the cantons reflect the diversity of Switzerland.

The cantons are responsible for many things that affect children directly, such as **school**. That is why holidays, curricula and school systems differ from canton to canton. The cantons also regulate the police, hospitals and part of the taxes themselves. This principle, that tasks are carried out as close to the people as possible, is called **federalism**.

In everyday life you can recognise the cantons in many places. Every car has a number plate with the **cantonal abbreviation**, for example ZH for Zurich, BE for Bern or TI for Ticino. In votes on changes to the Constitution, a majority of the cantons is needed as well as a majority of the people. In sport too, for example in Swiss wrestling, cantons often compete against each other.

begriffe.erklaerung: A state in which member states such as the cantons decide a lot for themselves.
The place where a canton's government and parliament have their seat.
The majority of the cantons in a vote.
Independent, with its own power.

gewusst: In the Federal Constitution the cantons are listed in a fixed order, which begins with Zurich, Bern and Lucerne and ends with the Jura.
In terms of area, the canton of the Grisons is almost 200 times the size of Basel-Stadt.
Every canton has its own cantonal anthem or song; some are over a hundred years old.

teile.einleitung: The Habeas Corpus Act is an English law of 1679. It protects people from being locked up without reason and without a trial. The idea behind it applies in many countries today, including Switzerland.
wichtigste: The English Parliament passed the Habeas Corpus Act in 1679.
It protects against arbitrary arrest.
“Habeas corpus” literally means: you shall have the body.
It was passed under King Charles II.
Abraham Lincoln partly suspended this right in 1861.
In Switzerland the idea is found in Article 31 of the Federal Constitution.
Article 5 of the ECHR also protects the right to have detention reviewed.

abschnitte.text: In **1679** the **English Parliament** passed the Habeas Corpus Act. The law set out more precisely an older legal remedy against **arbitrary detention**. The king at the time was **Charles II**, who reigned after the restoration of the monarchy. Parliament wanted to prevent the Crown from having people locked up as it pleased. The law is considered a milestone in the protection of personal freedom.

The Latin phrase **“habeas corpus”** literally means **“you shall have the body”**. It comes from the order to the jailer. He had to bring the prisoner **in person before the court**. The court then examined whether the detention was **lawful**. If it was not, the person was set free.

The core of the law is simple: nobody should be held for as long as someone likes without reason and without proceedings. Detention must be **reviewed quickly**. This idea is an important basis of the **rule of law**. It later influenced many constitutions and declarations of human rights, for example in the USA.

The **US Constitution** protects the right of habeas corpus. It only allows it to be suspended in cases of **rebellion or invasion**. During the **Civil War**, President **Abraham Lincoln** had the right suspended in parts of Maryland in April 1861. He wanted to prevent sabotage against the Union. This step was very controversial at the time.

In Switzerland **Article 31 of the Federal Constitution** regulates deprivation of liberty. Anyone taken into **pre-trial detention** has the right to be brought before a court without delay. The **European Convention on Human Rights** also protects this right. **Article 5 ECHR** lists the permitted reasons for detention exhaustively. Every person who is arrested has the right to a **review by a court**.

gewusst: Even the Magna Carta of 1215 contained the idea that nobody may be imprisoned without a lawful judgement.
In many countries, the term habeas corpus is still used today as the name for the right to have detention reviewed.

teile.einleitung: Inclusion means that all people belong and can take part. This also applies to people with a disability. Instead of someone having to adapt, the surroundings are designed so that they suit everyone.
wichtigste: With inclusion, everyone belongs and nobody is left out.
Blind people often read braille with their fingers.
A braille character has at most six dots.
Many deaf people communicate in sign language.
Ramps and lifts make buildings accessible for wheelchairs.
Athletes with disabilities compete at the Paralympics.
The International Day of Persons with Disabilities is on 3 December.

abschnitte.text: **Inclusion** comes from the Latin word for “to shut in” or include. All people should be able to take part at school, at work and in their free time. This concerns people with a **disability** in particular. Often even a small change helps everyone to take part. If a child in a wheelchair wants to join in, you can adapt the game so that they are included.

Many blind people read **braille**. It consists of raised dots that you feel with your fingers. Each character has room for **six dots** in two rows. It was invented by the Frenchman **Louis Braille**, who was blind himself. When walking, a white cane or a specially trained **guide dog** helps.

Many deaf people communicate in **sign language**. You speak with your hands, face and body. Sign languages are languages in their own right, with their own grammar. In German-speaking Switzerland there is **Swiss German Sign Language**; in French-speaking Switzerland and Ticino there are others. For some television programmes, interpreters translate into sign language.

Stairs are an obstacle for people in a **wheelchair**. **Ramps**, lifts and wide doors make buildings accessible for everyone. In Switzerland the **Disability Discrimination Act** has applied since 2004, and in 2014 Switzerland joined the **UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities**. In sport, athletes with disabilities compete at the **Paralympics**, which take place shortly after the Olympic Games. On **3 December**, a UN day draws attention to the rights of people with disabilities.

gewusst: Louis Braille developed his script when he was still a teenager.
On many medicine packets, the name is also written in braille.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Solothurn lies between the Jura and the Swiss Plateau. Its capital, Solothurn, is considered the most beautiful Baroque town in Switzerland. There the number 11 plays a special part.
wichtigste: In Solothurn the number 11 is considered the town's special number.
St Ursus Cathedral is dedicated to Saint Ursus.
The Weissenstein is Solothurn's local mountain.
Grenchen is a watchmaking town, and Olten an important railway junction.
During carnival, Solothurn is called “Honolulu”.

abschnitte.text: In the town of **Solothurn**, there are many things in elevens. People count, for example, eleven **fountains**, eleven churches and chapels and eleven towers. The cathedral has eleven bells, and its staircase has steps in groups of eleven. Solothurn was the **eleventh member** to join the Confederation, in 1481. That is why **11** is the town's number. There is even a clock with only eleven hours.

abschnitte.titel: A Baroque town with a cathedral
abschnitte.text: **St Ursus Cathedral** is dedicated to Saint **Ursus**. It is a splendid church from the 18th century. Solothurn is also called the **town of the ambassadors**. From 1530 to 1792, the ambassadors of the King of France lived here. That is why many splendid buildings were built in the **Baroque** style.

North of the town lies the **Verena Gorge**. There is a small chapel and a **hermitage** there. For centuries a hermit has lived there again and again. The local mountain is the **Weissenstein** in the Jura. A gondola goes up, and from the top you can see across the Swiss Plateau as far as the Alps.

**Grenchen** has had many **watch factories** for over 150 years, which is why it is called the watchmaking town. In **Olten** the railway lines from Zurich, Bern, Basel and Lucerne meet. Many people change trains there. During **carnival**, Solothurn becomes **“Honolulu”**. The name has long been part of the Solothurn carnival, and the jesters rule the town.

gewusst: The eleven-hour clock on Solothurn's market square has a dial with only eleven numbers.
The Aare flows through the middle of the town of Solothurn.

teile.einleitung: The canton of Thurgau lies in north-eastern Switzerland on Lake Constance. It is a canton with many fruit trees, fields and small villages. Its capital is Frauenfeld.
wichtigste: Thurgau is named after the River Thur.
Because of its many apple trees, it is also called Mostindien.
Thurgau has a long shore on Lake Constance.
A car ferry runs from Romanshorn to Friedrichshafen.
Kreuzlingen borders directly on the German town of Konstanz.

abschnitte.text: The **Thur** flows through the canton. The name Thurgau means **“area on the Thur”**. Thurgau has been a separate canton since **1803**; before that it was a subject territory of the Confederates. The capital is **Frauenfeld**. The **coat of arms** shows two golden lions. You can see the abbreviation **TG** on number plates.

A great many **apple trees** and **pear trees** grow in Thurgau. The apples are used to make **Most**, apple juice. That is why Thurgau is jokingly called **Mostindien** (Cider India). Some people also think the shape of the canton on the map looks like India. In spring the fruit trees blossom white and pink.

Thurgau has a long shore on **Lake Constance**. Towns such as **Arbon**, **Romanshorn** and **Kreuzlingen** lie there. A **car ferry** runs from Romanshorn to Friedrichshafen in Germany; the crossing takes about 40 minutes. **Kreuzlingen** and **Konstanz** have grown together. The national border runs directly between the two towns.

Near Frauenfeld lies **Ittingen Charterhouse**. **Carthusian monks** used to live there, spending much time in silence and prayer. Today there are gardens, museums, a farm and a hotel. **Arenenberg Castle** on the Untersee is also well known. The future French emperor Napoleon III lived there in his youth.

gewusst: Part of the border between Kreuzlingen and Konstanz is marked by works of art instead of a fence.
The Untersee is part of Lake Constance between Konstanz and Stein am Rhein.

teile.einleitung: With municipal tax, a municipality pays for many tasks that benefit everyone. In Switzerland each municipality decides for itself how high its tax is.
wichtigste: In Switzerland people pay taxes to the Confederation, the canton and the municipality.
With taxes, the municipality pays for schools, roads, the fire brigade and more.
Taxes are paid by adults with income or assets and by companies.
Those who earn more pay more tax.
The tax rate determines how high the municipal tax is.
Each municipality has its own tax rate.

abschnitte.text: The municipality has many tasks. It builds and runs **schools**, maintains **roads** and organises the **fire brigade**. For this it needs money, which comes mainly from **taxes**. State schools in Switzerland are free of charge. Exercise books and school materials are also paid for with taxes, so everyone pays for school together.

In Switzerland people pay taxes in **three places**: to the **Confederation**, the **canton** and the **municipality**. Each uses them to pay for its own tasks. Taxes are paid mainly by **adults** who earn money or have assets. **Companies** pay taxes too. Children without their own income do not pay any.

Every year adults fill in a **tax return**. In it they write down how much they earn and own. From this, the amount of tax they pay is calculated. Those who **earn more** pay more tax; those who earn little pay less. That way each person contributes according to their means.

Each municipality sets its own **tax rate**. This number shows how high the municipal tax is. A low tax rate means less tax. In many municipalities it is decided by the **voters** at the municipal assembly or by the municipal parliament. That is why people pay more or less tax depending on where they live.

gewusst: Two families with the same income can pay different amounts of tax depending on their municipality.
In many municipalities, voters decide themselves how high their tax is.
